title: Two glucose molecules join to make maltose
caption: A condensation reaction links carbon 1 of one α-glucose to carbon 4 of another through an oxygen: the α-1,4 glycosidic bond (shaded). One molecule of water is released, and hydrolysis, catalysed by maltase, reverses it.
alt: Two alpha-glucose molecules, C6H12O6, react to give maltose, C12H22O11, and a molecule of water.
description: Carbon 1 of one joins to carbon 4 of the other through an oxygen atom: an α-1,4 glycosidic bond.
A water molecule is released: this is a condensation reaction.
Atoms balance: C₁₂H₂₄O₁₂ on the left, C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ + H₂O on the right.
